title: 1967 Greater London Council election
summary: The Conservatives, led by Desmond Plummer, won a landslide 82 of the 100 seats — the first Conservative victory for a London-wide authority since 1931. Labour, hit by mid-term unpopularity under Harold Wilson's government, was reduced to just 18 seats.
highlights: First Conservative win for a London-wide body since 1931
Conservatives take control of the Inner London Education Authority

council.note: 100 councillors elected from borough-based multi-member electoral areas, plus 16 aldermen chosen by the council. Vote totals are all ballots cast under the multi-member bloc vote (each elector had one vote per seat); the percentage shares recorded by Rallings & Thrasher use a slightly different basis.
